1.1: And Yoshiyahu held the Feast of the Pesaḥ in Yerushalayim to his Aḏon, and offered the Pesaḥ on the fourteenth day of the first month;
1.2: having appointed the kohenim according to their daily services, being dressed in long garments, in the Hĕyḵal of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
1.3: And he spoke to the Lĕwites, the qodesh servants of Yisra’ĕl, that they should qadosh themselves to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to place the qodesh ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in the House that meleḵ Shelomoh the son of Dawiḏ had built.
1.4: And he said, “You shall no longer bear the ark upon your shoulders; now therefore serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, and serve His people Yisra’ĕl, and prepare yourselves according to your families and clans,
1.5: according to the order of Dawiḏ the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, and according to the splendor of his son Shelomoh. And stand in the Hĕyḵal according to the heads of the families of the Lĕwites, who serve in the presence of your brothers the children of Yisra’ĕl.
1.6: Slaughter the Pesaḥ in order, and prepare the offerings for your brothers, and guard the Pesaḥ according to the Command of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, which was given to Mosheh.”
1.7: And to the people who were found there, Yoshiyahu gave thirty thousand lambs and young goats, and three thousand calves; these were given to the people from the meleḵ’s allowance, according to his promise, to the kohenim, and to the Lĕwites.
1.8: And Ḥilqiyahu, Zeḵaryah, and Yeḥi’ĕl, the governors of the Hĕyḵal, gave to the kohenim two thousand six hundred sheep, and three hundred calves for the Pesaḥ.
1.9: And Yeḵonyah and Shemayah and Nethan’ĕl his brother and Ḥashaḇyah, and Aḥi’ĕl and Yoram, captains over thousands, gave to the Lĕwites five thousand sheep, and seven hundred calves for the Pesaḥ.
1.10: And when these were done, the kohenim and Lĕwites, having the unleavened bread, stood in proper order according to their clans,
1.11: and according to the nobility of the fathers before the people, to offer to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, as it is written in the Book of Mosheh. And thus they did in the morning,
1.12: and they roasted the Pesaḥ with fire, as required. As for the slaughterings, they boiled them in bronze pots and cauldrons with a pleasing flavor,
1.13: and put them before all the people; and afterward they prepared for themselves, and for the kohenim their brothers, the sons of Aharon.
1.14: For the kohenim offered the fat until evening, and the Lĕwites prepared for themselves, and their brothers the kohenim, the sons of Aharon.
1.15: Also the qodesh singers, the sons of Asaph, were in their service, according to the appointment of Dawiḏ, that is: Asaph, Zeḵaryah, and Yeḏuthun, who were of the meleḵ’s servants.
1.16: And the gatekeepers were at every gate - it was not lawful for any to go from his regular service - for their brothers the Lĕwites prepared for them.
1.17: Thus the matters which pertained to the slaughterings of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 were accomplished on that day, that they might hold the Pesaḥ,
1.18: and offer slaughterings upon the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, according to the command of meleḵ Yoshiyahu.
1.19: So the children of Yisra’ĕl who were present held the Pesaḥ at that time, and the Feast of Matstsoth seven days;
1.20: and such a Pesaḥ was not kept in Yisra’ĕl since the time of the naḇi Shemu’ĕl.
1.21: Even all the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl did not keep such a Pesaḥ as Yoshiyahu, and the kohenim and the Lĕwites and the Yahuḏim held with all Yisra’ĕl who were found dwelling at Yerushalayim.
1.22: In the eighteenth year of the reign of Yoshiyahu this Pesaḥ was kept.
1.23: And the works of Yoshiyahu were upright before his Aḏon with a reverent heart.
1.24: As for that which came to be in his time, they were written in former times, concerning those who sinned, and acted wickedly against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 above all people and reigns, and how they grieved Him exceedingly, so that the words of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 rose up against Yisra’ĕl.
1.25: Now after all these acts of Yoshiyahu, it came to be that Pharaoh the meleḵ of Mitsrayim came to battle at Karkemish on the Perath; and Yoshiyahu went out against him.
1.26: But the meleḵ of Mitsrayim sent to him, saying, “What have I to do with you, O meleḵ of Yahuḏah?
1.27: I am not sent out against you by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim; for my battle is at Perath. And now indeed, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is with me. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is with me urging me forward. Depart from me, and do not be against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
1.28: However Yoshiyahu did not turn back his chariot from him, but undertook to fight with him, not regarding the words of the naḇi Yirmeyahu spoken by the mouth of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄;
1.29: but joined in battle against him in the plain of Meḡiddo, and the princes came against meleḵ Yoshiyahu.
1.30: Then the meleḵ said to his servants, “Carry me away out of the battle; for I am very weak.” And immediately his servants took him away out of the battle.
1.31: Then mounting his second chariot, and being brought back to Yerushalayim, he died and was buried in his father’s tomb;
1.32: and all the Yahuḏim mourned for Yoshiyahu. Also Yirmeyahu the naḇi lamented for Yoshiyahu, and the chief men with the women made lamentation for him to this day. And this was ordained for a law to be done continually in all the nation of Yisra’ĕl.
1.33: These are written in the Book of the Annals of the melaḵim of Yahuḏah, and every one of the acts that Yoshiyahu did, and his esteem and his understanding in the Law of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and that which he had done before and these now reported, are written in the Book of the Melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl and Yahuḏah.
1.34: And the people took Yaho’aḥaz the son of Yoshiyahu, and made him meleḵ instead of Yoshiyahu his father, when he was twenty-three years old.
1.35: And he reigned in Yahuḏah and in Yerushalayim three months; and then the meleḵ of Mitsrayim removed him from the reign in Yerushalayim.
1.36: And he placed a tax over the land of a hundred kiḵars of silver and one kiḵar of gold.
1.37: The meleḵ of Mitsrayim also made meleḵ Yahoyaqim his brother meleḵ of Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim.
1.38: And Yahoyaqim imprisoned the nobles, but he seized Tseruyah his brother, and brought him out of Mitsrayim.
1.39: Yahoyaqim was twenty-five years old when he was made meleḵ in the land of Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim; and he did evil before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
1.40: Therefore Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar the meleḵ of Baḇel came up against him, and bound him with chains of bronze, and carried him away to Baḇel.
1.41: Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar also took the qodesh vessels of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and carried them away, and put them in his own temple at Baḇel.
1.42: And those matters that are written concerning him, and of his uncleanness and unrighteousness, are written in the annals of the melaḵim.
1.43: And Yoyaqim his son reigned in his place; he was made meleḵ being eighteen years old;
1.44: and he reigned only three months and ten days in Yerushalayim; and did evil before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
1.45: So after a year, Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar sent and had him brought to Baḇel along with the qodesh vessels of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
1.46: and made Tsiḏqiyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim, when he was twenty-one years old; and he reigned eleven years.
1.47: And he also did evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and took no heed of the words that were spoken to him by the naḇi Yirmeyahu from the mouth of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
1.48: And after meleḵ Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar had made him swear by the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, he broke his oath, and rebelled; and hardening his neck and his heart, he transgressed the Laws of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl.
1.49: The governors of the people and of the kohenim also did much against the Laws, and surpassed all the abominations of the other nations, and defiled the Hĕyḵal of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, which was qadosh in Yerushalayim.
1.50: Nevertheless the Elohim of their fathers sent His messenger to call them back, because He spared them and also His Mishkan.
1.51: But they mocked His messengers; and see, when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to them, they mocked His neḇi’im
1.52: so much that He, being wroth with His people for their great unrighteousness, commanded the melaḵim of the Kasdites to come up against them;
1.53: who slew their young men with the sword, even also within the surroundings of their qodesh Hĕyḵal, and spared neither young man nor maiden, old man nor child among them; for He delivered all into their hands.
1.54: And they took all the qodesh vessels of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, both small and great, with the vessels of the ark of Elohim, and the meleḵ’s treasures, and carried them away to Baḇel.
1.55: As for the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, they burned it, and broke down the walls of Yerushalayim, and lit her towers on fire.
1.56: And as for her esteemed objects, they never ceased till they had consumed and brought them all to naught. And the people that were not slain with the sword, he carried to Baḇel,
1.57: who became servants to him and his children, till the Parasians reigned, to fill the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoken by the mouth of Yirmeyahu:
1.58: “Until the land had enjoyed her Shabbathoth. As long as she lay waste she kept Shabbath, until seventy years were completed.”

2.1: In the first year of Koresh meleḵ of Paras, in order to accomplish the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 by the mouth of Yirmeyahu,
2.2: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 stirred up the spirit of Koresh meleḵ of Paras, so that he called out in all his reign, and also put it in writing,
2.3: saying, “Thus said Koresh meleḵ of Paras; 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of Yisra’ĕl, the Most High Ĕl, has made me meleḵ of the whole world,
2.4: and commanded me to build Him a House at Yerushalayim in Yahuḏah.
2.5: “If therefore there are any of you who are of His people, let 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, even his Aḏon, be with him, and let him go up to Yerushalayim that is in Yahuḏah, and build the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of Yisra’ĕl, for He is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who dwells in Yerushalayim.
2.6: “Whoever then dwells in the places round about, I say, let them help him - those who are his neighbors - with gold and with silver,
2.7: with gifts, with horses and with cattle, and other goods which have been presented with a vow, for the Hĕyḵal of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 at Yerushalayim.”
2.8: Then the chiefs of the families of Yahuḏah and of the tribe of Binyamin stood up; the kohenim also, and the Lĕwites and all those whose heart 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had moved to go up and to build a House for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 at Yerushalayim.
2.9: And those who dwelt round about them helped them in all matters with silver and gold, with horses and cattle, and with very many gifts of a great number whose hearts were stirred up to do so.
2.10: meleḵ Koresh also brought out the qodesh vessels, which Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar had carried away from Yerushalayim, and had put up in his temple of idols.
2.11: Now when Koresh meleḵ of Paras had brought them out, he delivered them to Mithreḏath his treasurer;
2.12: And by him they were delivered to Shĕshbatstsar the governor of Yahuḏah.
2.13: And this was the number of them: one thousand gold cups, and one thousand of silver, twenty-nine silver fire holders, thirty bowls of gold, and two thousand four hundred and ten of silver, and one thousand other vessels.
2.14: So all the vessels of gold and of silver which were carried away, were five thousand four hundred and sixty-nine.
2.15: These were brought back by Shĕshbatstsar, together with those in captivity, from Baḇel to Yerushalayim.
2.16: But in the time of Artaḥshashta meleḵ of Paras Bishlam, and Mithreḏath, and Taḇe’ĕl, and Reḥum the governor, and Shimshai the scribe, with others that were in commission with them dwelling in Shomeron and other places, wrote to him against those who dwelt in Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim these following words:
2.17: To meleḵ Artaḥshashta our master, your servants - Reḥum the governor, and Shimshai the scribe and the rest of their council and the judges that are in Koĕlĕ-Suria and Phoinikĕ.
2.18: Let it be known to our master the meleḵ, that the Yahuḏim who came up from you to us, having come to Yerushalayim, that rebellious and wicked city, are building the marketplaces, and repairing the walls of it and laying the foundation of the Hĕyḵal.
2.19: Now if this city and its walls are built up again, they shall not only refuse to give tribute, but also rebel against melaḵim.
2.20: And because that which pertains to the Hĕyḵal are now in hand, we think it right not to neglect such a matter,
2.21: but to speak to our master the meleḵ, to the intent that, if it be your pleasure, it may be sought out in the books of your fathers;
2.22: and you shall find in the annals which are written concerning these matters, and shall understand that this city was rebellious, troubling both melaḵim and cities;
2.23: and that the Yahuḏim were rebellious, and raised continuous wars; which is the very reason this city was made desolate.
2.24: Therefore we do now declare unto you, O master the meleḵ, that if this city be built again, and its walls rebuilt, you shall no longer have passage into Koĕlĕ-Suria and Phoinikĕ.
2.25: Then the meleḵ wrote back again to Reḥum the governor, to Shimshai the scribe, and to the rest of their companions, and dwellers in Shomeron and Suria and Phoinikĕ, after this manner:
2.26: I have read the letter which you have sent to me; therefore I commanded to make diligent search, and it has been found that this city was from the beginning exercising against melaḵim;
2.27: And the men within were given to rebellion and fighting, and that mighty and harsh melaḵim were in Yerushalayim, who reigned and exacted tributes in Koĕlĕ-Suria and Phoinikĕ.
2.28: Now therefore I have commanded to prevent those men from building the city, and take heed that there be no more done in it;
2.29: and that those wicked workers proceed no further to the annoyance of melaḵim.
2.30: Then when the letter from meleḵ Artaḥshashta had been read, Reḥum and Shimshai the scribe and the rest of their companions hurried to Yerushalayim with a troop of horsemen, and a crowd of people in battle array began to hinder the builders; and the building of the Hĕyḵal in Yerushalayim ceased until the second year of the reign of Dareyawesh meleḵ of Paras.

3.1: Now when Dareyawesh reigned, he made a great feast for all his subjects and for all his household and for all the princes of Maḏai and Paras,
3.2: and for all the governors and captains and viceroys that were under him, from Hodu to Kush, in a hundred and twenty-seven provinces.
3.3: And when they had eaten and drank, and being satisfied had gone home, then Dareyawesh the meleḵ went into his bedroom and slept, and soon after awoke.
3.4: Then three young men who were of the guards that guarded the meleḵ personally spoke one to another,
3.5: “Let each one of us speak a word of that which is strongest, and whose words shall seem wiser than the others, to him shall the meleḵ Dareyawesh give great gifts, and great esteem in overcoming;
3.6: to be clothed in purple, to drink from gold, and to sleep on gold, and a chariot with bridles of gold, and a turban of fine linen, and a chain about his neck.
3.7: “And he shall sit next to Dareyawesh because of his wisdom, and shall be called a relative of Dareyawesh.”
3.8: And then every one wrote his words, sealed it, and laid it under the pillow of meleḵ Dareyawesh;
3.9: and said, “When the meleḵ has risen, someone shall give him the writings; and of whose side the meleḵ and the three princes of Paras shall judge his words to be the wisest, he shall have overcome, as was agreed.”
3.10: The first wrote: Wine is the strongest.
3.11: The second wrote: The meleḵ is strongest.
3.12: The third wrote: Women are strongest; but above all, truth shall overcome.
3.13: Now when the meleḵ had risen, they took their writings, and delivered them to him, and so he read them.
3.14: And having sent, he called all the princes of Paras and Maḏai, and the governors, and the captains, and the viceroys, and the chief officers;
3.15: and he sat down on the royal seat of judgment; and the writings were read before them.
3.16: And he said, “Call the young men, and they shall declare their own words.” So they were called, and came in.
3.17: And he said to them, “Speak to us your thoughts concerning the writings.” Then the first, who had spoken of the strength of wine, began,
3.18: and he said, “O you men, how exceedingly strong is wine! It causes all men who drink it to stray.
3.19: “It makes the mind of the meleḵ and of the fatherless child to all be equal; of the slave and the free, of the poor and the wealthy.
3.20: “It also turns every thought into joy and rejoicing, so that a man remembers neither sorrow nor debt,
3.21: and it brings wealth to every heart, so that a man remembers neither meleḵ nor governor; and it causes to speak of all in coins.
3.22: “And when they are in their cups, they forget their love to both friends and brothers, and a little after draw out swords.
3.23: “But when they are from the wine, they do not remember what they have done.
3.24: “O you men, is not wine, that forces to do this, the strongest?” And when he had so spoken, he remained silent.

4.1: Then the second, that had spoken of the strength of the meleḵ, began to speak:
4.2: “O you men, do not men who reign over sea and land and all in them excel in strength?
4.3: “And yet the meleḵ is mightier; for he is master of all these, and rules over them, and whatever he commands them they do.
4.4: “If he commands them to fight, one against the other, they do it; if he sends them out against their enemies, they go, and tear down mountains, walls and towers.
4.5: “They slay and are slain, but do not disobey the meleḵ’s command. If they overcome, they bring all to the meleḵ, as well the spoil, and all other matters.
4.6: “Likewise for those who are not soldiers, and have naught to do with wars, but are farmers; when they have reaped again that which they had sown, they bring it to the meleḵ, and compel one another to pay tribute to the meleḵ.
4.7: “And yet he is but one man. If he commands to kill, they kill; if he commands to spare, they spare;
4.8: “If he commands to smite, they smite; if he commands to destroy, they destroy; if he commands to build, they build;
4.9: if he commands to cut down, they cut down; if he commands to plant, they plant.
4.10: “So all his people and his armies obey him; furthermore he lies down, he eats and drinks, and takes his rest,
4.11: and these keep watch around about him, neither may anyone depart, and do his own business, nor do they disobey him in any matter.
4.12: “O you men, how should not the meleḵ be mightiest, when he is obeyed in such a way?” And he kept silent.
4.13: Then the third, who had spoken of women, and of the truth - this was Zerubbaḇel - began to speak:
4.14: “O you men, it is not the great meleḵ, nor the crowd of men, neither is it wine that excels. Who is it then that rules them, or has the rulership over them? Are they not women?
4.15: “Women have borne the meleḵ and all the people that reign by sea and land.
4.16: “Even from them they have come, and they nourished those who planted the vineyards, from where the wine comes.
4.17: “These also make garments for men; these bring esteem to men, and without women, men cannot be.
4.18: “Indeed, and if men have gathered together gold and silver, or any other luxury, do they not love a woman who is lovely in appearance and loveliness?
4.19: “And letting all those go, do they not gape, and even with open mouth fix their eyes fast on her; and do not all men have more desire for her than for silver or gold, or any luxury whatever?
4.20: “A man leaves his own father who raised him, and his own land, and clings to his wife.
4.21: “He does not remain, and remembers neither father, nor mother, nor land, to spend his life with his wife.
4.22: “By this you also must know that women have rule over you. Do you not labor and toil, and bring and give all to the woman?
4.23: “Indeed, a man takes his sword, and goes his way to rob and to steal, to sail over the sea and upon rivers,
4.24: and faces a lion, and goes in the darkness; and when he has stolen, plundered, and robbed, he brings it to his love.
4.25: “Therefore a man loves his wife better than father or mother.
4.26: “Indeed, there are many that have lost their minds for women, and become servants for their sakes.
4.27: “Many also have perished, have strayed, and sinned, for women.
4.28: “And now do you not believe me? Is not the meleḵ great in his power? Do not all countries fear to touch him?
4.29: “Yet I saw him and Apamĕ the meleḵ’s concubine, the daughter of the admirable Bartakos, sitting at the right hand of the meleḵ,
4.30: and taking the crown from the meleḵ’s head, and putting it upon her own head; she also struck the meleḵ with her left hand.
4.31: “And yet for all this the meleḵ gaped and gazed upon her with open mouth. If she laughed at him, he laughed also; but if she took any displeasure in him, the meleḵ was eager to flatter, that she might be reconciled to him again.
4.32: “O you men, how could it be but women are strongest, seeing they do this?”
4.33: Then the meleḵ and the princes looked at each other, so he began to speak of the truth:
4.34: “O you men, are not women strong? Great is the earth, high is the shamayim, swift is the sun in its course, for it makes the circuit of the shamayim, and follows its course again to its own place in one day.
4.35: “Is He who makes these not great? Therefore the truth is great, and stronger than all.
4.36: “All the earth calls upon the truth, and the shamayim baraḵ it. All works shake and tremble at it, and there is no unrighteousness with it.
4.37: “Wine is wicked, the meleḵ is wicked, women are wicked, all the children of men are wicked, and such are all their wicked works and there is no truth in them, and in their unrighteousness they shall also perish.
4.38: “As for the truth, it endures, and is always strong; it lives and overcomes forever.
4.39: “With her there is no partiality or preference; but she does that which is righteous, and refrains from all unrighteousness and wickedness; and all men approve of her works.
4.40: “Nor is there any unrighteousness in her judgment; but she is the strength, reign, power, and excellence, of all ages. Baruḵ be the Elohim of truth.”
4.41: And with that he remained silent. And all the people then shouted, and said, “Great is Truth, and strongest of all!”
4.42: Then the meleḵ said to him, “Ask what you would, more than what is appointed in the writing, and we shall give it to you, because you have been found wisest; and you shall sit next to me, and shall be called my relative.”
4.43: Then he said to the meleḵ, “Remember your vow to build Yerushalayim, which you swore in the day when you came to your reign,
4.44: and to send all the vessels that were taken away from Yerushalayim, which Koresh put aside, when he vowed to destroy Baḇel, and to send them there again.
4.45: “You have also vowed to rebuild the Hĕyḵal, which the Eḏomites burned when Yahuḏah was laid waste by the Kasdites.
4.46: “And now, O master the meleḵ, this is that which I require, and which I desire from you, and this is the princely kindness proceeding from yourself: I desire therefore that you fulfill the vow, the works of which you have vowed with your own mouth to the Meleḵ of the shamayim.”
4.47: Then Dareyawesh the meleḵ stood up, and kissed him, and wrote letters for him to all the treasurers and viceroys and captains and governors, that they should safely transfer both he, and all those who would go up with him to rebuild Yerushalayim.
4.48: He also wrote letters to the viceroys that were in Koĕlĕ-Suria and Phoinikĕ, and to those in Leḇanon, that they should bring cedar wood from Leḇanon to Yerushalayim, and that they should build the city with him.
4.49: And he wrote for all the Yahuḏim that went out of his reign up into Yahuḏah, concerning their freedom, that no officer, no ruler, no viceroy, nor treasurer, should forcibly enter into their doors;
4.50: and that all the land which they hold should be free without tribute; and that the Eḏomites should give up the villages of the Yahuḏim which they held;
4.51: even that there should be given twenty kiḵars yearly toward the building of the Hĕyḵal, until the time that it was built;
4.52: and another ten kiḵars yearly, to maintain the burnt offerings on the altar every day, for they had a Command to offer seventeen;
4.53: and that all those who went from Baḇel to build the city should have freedom, they as well as their descendants, and all the kohenim that went away.
4.54: He also wrote concerning their support, and the garments of the kohenim in which they serve;
4.55: and also for the support of the Lĕwites to be given to them until the day that the House was finished, and Yerushalayim built up.
4.56: And he commanded to give land and wages to all who guarded the city.
4.57: He also sent away all the vessels from Baḇel that Koresh had put aside; and all that Koresh had commanded to be given, he also commanded the same to be done, and sent to Yerushalayim.
4.58: Now when the young man went out, he lifted up his face to the shamayim toward Yerushalayim, and baraḵ the Meleḵ of the shamayim,
4.59: and said, “From You comes deliverance, from You comes wisdom, and Yours is the esteem, and I am Your servant.
4.60: “Baruḵ are You, who has given me wisdom; for I give thanks to You, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of our fathers.”
4.61: And so he took the letters, and went out, and came to Baḇel, and told all his brothers,
4.62: and they baraḵ the Elohim of their fathers, because He had given them release and freedom
4.63: to go up, and to build Yerushalayim, and the Hĕyḵal which is called by His Name. And they feasted with musical instruments and gladness seven days.

5.1: After this the heads of the families were chosen according to their tribes, to go up with their wives and sons and daughters, with their male servants and female servants, and their cattle.
5.2: And Dareyawesh sent a thousand horsemen with them, till they had brought them back to Yerushalayim safely, and with musical instruments, tambourines and flutes.
5.3: And all their brothers played, and he made them go up together with them.
5.4: And these are the names of the men who went up, according to their families among their tribes, after their several heads.
5.5: The kohenim, the sons of Pineḥas the son of Aharon: Yĕshua the son of Yotsaḏaq, the son of Serayah, and Yoyaqim the son of Zerubbaḇel, the son of She’alti’ĕl, of the house of Dawiḏ, from the relatives of Perets, of the tribe of Yahuḏah;
5.6: who spoke wise words before Dareyawesh the meleḵ of Paras in the second year of his reign, in the month of Nisan, which is the first month.
5.7: And these are those of the Yahuḏim who came up from the captivity, where they dwelt as foreigners, whom Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar the meleḵ of Baḇel had carried away to Baḇel.
5.8: And they returned to Yerushalayim, and to the other parts of Yahuḏah, every man to his own city, who came with Zerubbaḇel, with Yĕshua, Neḥemyah and Zeḵaryah and Serayah, Naḥamani, Mordeḵai, Bilshan, Mispar, Re’ĕlayah, Reḥum, and Ba’anah, their guides.
5.9: The number of those of the nation, and their governors: sons of Parosh, two thousand one hundred and seventy-two; the sons of Shaphat, four hundred and seventy-two;
5.10: the sons of Araḥ, seven hundred and fifty-six;
5.11: the sons of Paḥath-Mo’aḇ, two thousand eight hundred and twelve;
5.12: the sons of Ĕylam, one thousand two hundred and fifty-four; the sons of Zattu, nine hundred and forty-five; the sons of Zakkai, seven hundred and five; the sons of Bani, six hundred and forty-eight;
5.13: the sons of Bĕḇai, six hundred and twenty-three; the sons of Azgaḏ, three thousand two hundred and twenty-two;
5.14: the sons of Aḏoniqam, six hundred and sixty-seven; the sons of Biḡwai, two thousand and sixty-six; the sons of Aḏin, four hundred and fifty-four;
5.15: the sons of Atĕr of Ḥizqiyah, ninety-two; the sons of Kilan and Azetah sixty-seven; the sons of Azzur, four hundred and thirty-two;
5.16: the sons of Ḥananyah, one hundred and one; the sons of Arom, thirty-two; and the sons of Bĕsai, three hundred and twenty-three; the sons of Ḥariph, one hundred and two;
5.17: the sons of Bether, three thousand and five; the sons of Bĕyth Leḥem, one hundred and twenty-three:
5.18: those of Netophah, fifty-five; those of Anathoth, one hundred and fifty-eight; those of Bĕyth Shemesh, forty-two;
5.19: those of Qiryathayim, twenty-five; those of Kephirah and Be’ĕroth, seven hundred and forty-three; those of Pira, seven hundred;
5.20: those of Qaḏĕsh and Ḥumtah, four hundred and twenty-two; those of Ramah and Geḇa, six hundred and twenty-one;
5.21: those of Maḥlon, one hundred and twenty-two; those of Bĕyth Ĕl, fifty-two; the sons of Naphish, one hundred and fifty-six;
5.22: the sons of Loḏ, Ḥaḏiḏ and Ono, seven hundred and twenty-five; the sons of Yeriḥo, two hundred and forty-five;
5.23: the sons of Sena’ah, three thousand three hundred and thirty.
5.24: The kohenim: the sons of Yeḏayah, the son of Yĕshua among the sons of Elyashiḇ, nine hundred and seventy-two; the sons of Immĕr, one thousand and fifty-two;
5.25: The sons of Pashḥur, one thousand and forty-seven; the sons of Ḥarim, one thousand and seventeen.
5.26: The Lĕwites: the sons of Yĕshua, and Qaḏmi’ĕl, and Ba’anah, and Hoḏawyah, seventy-four.
5.27: The qodesh singers: the sons of Asaph, one hundred and twenty-eight.
5.28: The gatekeepers: the sons of Shallum, the sons of Atĕr, the sons of Talmon, the sons of Aqquḇ, the sons of Ḥatita, the sons of Shoḇai, one hundred and thirty-nine in all.
5.29: The Nethinim: the sons of Tsiḥa, the sons of Ḥasupha, the sons of Tabba’oth, the sons of Qĕros, the sons of Si’aha, the sons of Paḏon, the sons of Leḇanah, the sons of Ḥaḡaḇah,
5.30: the sons of Aqquḇ, the sons of Uzza, the sons of Kataḇ, the sons of Ḥaḡaḇ, the sons of Shamlai, the sons of Ḥanan, the sons of Giddĕl, the sons of Gaḥar,
5.31: the sons of Re’ayah, the sons of Retsin, the sons of Neqoḏa, the sons of Ḥashuḇah, the sons of Gazzam, the sons of Uzza, the sons of Pasĕaḥ, the sons of Azaryah, the sons of Bĕsai, the sons of Asnah, the sons of Me’unim, the sons of Nephusim, the sons of Baqbuq, the sons of Ḥaqupha, the sons of Ḥarḥur, the sons of Pharaqim, the sons of Batsluth,
5.32: the sons of Meḥiḏa, the sons of Kutha, the sons of Ḥarsha, the sons of Barqos, the sons of Sisera, the sons of Tĕmaḥ, the sons of Netsiyaḥ, the sons of Ḥatipha.
5.33: The sons of the servants of Shelomoh: the sons of Sophereth, the sons of Peruḏa, the sons of Ya’ala, the sons of Darqon, the sons of Yisra’ĕl, the sons of Shephatyah,
5.34: the sons of Ḥattil, the sons of Poḵereth, the sons of Tseḇayim, the sons of Tsereth, the sons of Masias, the sons of Gar, the sons of Addus, the sons of Tsoḇa, the sons of Apherra, the sons of Barodis, the sons of Sheḇat, the sons of Allon.
5.35: All the Nethinim, and the sons of the servants of Shelomoh, were three hundred and seventy-two.
5.36: These came up from Tĕl Melaḥ and Tĕl Ḥarsha, Keruḇ, Addan, and Immĕr;
5.37: though could not show their families, nor their seed, how they were of Yisra’ĕl: the sons of Delayah, the son of Toḇiyah, the sons of Neqoḏa, six hundred and fifty-two.
5.38: And of the kohenim that assumed the office of the kehunnah, and were not found: the sons of Ḥaḇayah, the sons of Qots, the sons of Yaddua, who married Ḥaggiyah one of the daughters of Barzillai, and was named after his name.
5.39: And when the genealogy of the relatives of these men was sought in the register, and was not found, they were removed from performing the office of the kehunnah;
5.40: for Neḥemyah the governor said to them that they should not be partakers of the qodesh matters, till there rose up a kohĕn ha’gadol wearing the Urim and the Tummim.
5.41: So from those twelve years old and upward of Yisra’ĕl, besides male and female servants, all numbered forty two thousand three hundred and sixty.
5.42: Their male and female servants were seven thousand three hundred and forty-seven; the male and female singers, two hundred and forty-five;
5.43: four hundred and thirty-five camels, seven thousand and thirty-six horses, two hundred and forty-five mules, five thousand five hundred and twenty-five beasts for the yoke.
5.44: And some of the chiefs of their families, when they came to the Hĕyḵal of Elohim that is in Yerushalayim, vowed to put up the House again in its place according to their ability,
5.45: and to give into the qodesh treasury, one thousand minas of gold, five thousand of silver for the work, and one hundred garments for the kehunnah.
5.46: And so the kohenim and the Lĕwites and the people dwelt in Yerushalayim, and in the land; also the singers and the gatekeepers, and all Yisra’ĕl in their villages.
5.47: But when the seventh month came, and when the children of Yisra’ĕl were each in his own place, they all came together with one accord into the open place of the first gate which is toward the east.
5.48: Then Yĕshua the son of Yotsaḏaq stood up, and his brothers the kohenim and Zerubbaḇel the son of She’alti’ĕl, and his brothers, and prepared the altar of the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl,
5.49: to offer burnt offerings upon it according to the Command in the Book of Mosheh, the man of Elohim.
5.50: And some from the other nations of the land were gathered to them. And they put up the altar in its place, because all the nations of the land were at enmity with them, and oppressed them; and they brought offerings at the appointed times, and burnt offerings to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 both morning and evening.
5.51: They also held the Feast of Sukkoth, as it is commanded in the Torah, and brought offerings daily, as appointed.
5.52: And after that, the continual offerings, and the offering of the Shabbathoth, and of the new moons, and of all qodesh Feasts.
5.53: And all those who had made any vow to Elohim began to offer offerings to Elohim from the first day of the seventh month, although the Hĕyḵal of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had not yet been built.
5.54: And they gave silver, food and drink to the masons and carpenters with gladness.
5.55: To those of Tsiḏon and Tsor they also gave by weight, that they should bring cedars from Leḇanon, which would be brought by boat to the harbor of Yapho, according to the command given them by Koresh meleḵ of Paras.
5.56: And in the second year and second month after their coming to the Hĕyḵal of Elohim at Yerushalayim, Zerubbaḇel the son of She’alti’ĕl, and Yĕshua the son of Yotsaḏaq, and their brothers, and the kohenim, and the Lĕwites began, and all those who had come to Yerushalayim out of the captivity;
5.57: and they laid the foundation of the House of Elohim on the first day of the second month, in the second year after they had come to Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim.
5.58: And they appointed the Lĕwites from twenty years old over the works of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. Then Yĕshua stood up, and his sons and brothers, and Qaḏmi’ĕl his brother, and the sons of Mĕyḏeḇa, with the sons of Yaḏa the son of Elyaḏa, with their sons and brothers; all Lĕwites, with one accord pressed forward with the work, laboring to advance the work on the House of Elohim. So the workmen built the Hĕyḵal of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
5.59: And the kohenim stood dressed in their garments with musical instruments and trumpets; and the Lĕwites, the sons of Asaph had cymbals,
5.60: as they sang songs of thanksgiving and baraḵ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, as directed by Dawiḏ the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl.
5.61: And they sang songs to the praise of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with loud voices, because His kindness and esteem in all Yisra’ĕl is forever.
5.62: And all the people sounded trumpets, and shouted with a loud voice, singing songs of thanksgiving to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for the raising of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
5.63: Also of the kohenim and Lĕwites, and of the chief of their families, the elders who had seen the former House came to the building with crying and great weeping.
5.64: And many with trumpets and joy shouted with a loud voice,
5.65: so that the trumpets could not be heard for the weeping of the people; yet the crowd sounded greatly, so that it was heard from afar.
5.66: Therefore when the enemies of the tribe of Yahuḏah and Binyamin heard it, they came to know what the noise of trumpets meant.
5.67: And they perceived that those who were from the captivity had built the Hĕyḵal to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl.
5.68: So they went to Zerubbaḇel and Yĕshua, and to the heads of the families, and said to them, “We shall build together with you,
5.69: for we also, as you, obey your Aḏon, and have slaughtered to Him from the days of Ĕsarḥaddon the meleḵ of Ashshur, who brought us here.”
5.70: Then Zerubbaḇel and Yĕshua and the heads of the families of Yisra’ĕl said to them, “It is not for you and us to build a House to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim together.
5.71: “We ourselves alone shall build to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of Yisra’ĕl, according to the command given us by Koresh the meleḵ of Paras.”
5.72: But the foreigners of the land relying heavily on the inhabitants of Yahuḏah, and restricting their supplies, hindered their building;
5.73: and by their secret schemes, and popular persuasions and unrest, they hindered the completion of the building the whole time that meleḵ Koresh lived; so they were hindered from building for the space of two years, until the reign of Dareyawesh.

6.1: Now in the second year of the reign of Dareyawesh Ḥaggai and Zeḵaryah the son of Iddo, the neḇi’im, naḇa to the Yahuḏim in Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, which was upon them.
6.2: Then Zerubbaḇel the son of She’alti’ĕl stood up, and Yĕshua the son of Yotsaḏaq, and began to build the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 at Yerushalayim, assisted by the neḇi’im of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who were with them.
6.3: At the same time Tattenai the governor of Suria came to them and Phoinikĕ, with Shethar-Bozenai and his companions, and said to them,
6.4: “By whose decree do you build this House and this roof, and doing all these other matters? And who are the workmen that perform these?”
6.5: Nevertheless the elders of the Yahuḏim obtained favor, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had overseen the captivity;
6.6: and they were not hindered from building, until such time as word was given to Dareyawesh concerning them, and an answer received.
6.7: The copy of the letters which Tattenai, governor of Suria and Phoinikĕ, and Shethar-Bozenai, with their companions, rulers in Suria and Phoinikĕ, wrote and sent to Dareyawesh: To meleḵ Dareyawesh, greetings.
6.8: Let all matters be known to our master the meleḵ, that having come into the land of Yahuḏah, and entered into the city of Yerushalayim we found in the city of Yerushalayim the elders of the Yahuḏim who were of the captivity
6.9: building a great and new House to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, of hewn and costly stones, and the timber already laid upon the walls.
6.10: And those works are done with great speed, and the work is prospering in their hands, and being done with all esteem and diligence.
6.11: Then we asked these elders, saying, “By whose command are you building this House, and laying the foundations of these works?”
6.12: Therefore with the purpose that we might make known to you in writing, we demanded of those who were the chief workers, and we required from them the names of their heads in writing.
6.13: So they gave us this answer, “We are the servants of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who made the shamayim and earth.
6.14: “And as for this House, it was built many years ago by a great and strong meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, and was finished.
6.15: “But when our fathers provoked Elohim to wrath, and sinned against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of Yisra’ĕl who is in the shamayim, He gave them over to the power of Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel, of the Kasdites;
6.16: who pulled down the House, and burned it, and carried away the people captive to Baḇel.
6.17: “But in the first year that meleḵ Koresh reigned over the land of Baḇel, Koresh the meleḵ wrote to build up this House.
6.18: “And the qodesh vessels of gold and silver that Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar had carried away out of the House at Yerushalayim, and had put them in his own temple; these Koresh the meleḵ brought out again from the temple at Baḇel, and they were delivered to Zerubbaḇel and to Shĕshbatstsar the ruler
6.19: with orders that he should take these same vessels, and put them in the Hĕyḵal at Yerushalayim; and that the Hĕyḵal of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 should be built in its place.
6.20: “Then the same Shĕshbatstsar, having come here, laid the foundations of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 at Yerushalayim; and from that time to this, is still under construction; it is not yet fully complete.
6.21: “Now therefore, if it seems good to the meleḵ, let a search be made among the records of meleḵ Koresh;
6.22: and if it is found that the building of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 at Yerushalayim has been done with the consent of meleḵ Koresh, and if our master the meleḵ approves, let him inform us of this.”
6.23: Then meleḵ Dareyawesh commanded to search among the records at Baḇel; and so at Aḥmetha the palace, which is in the land of Maḏai, there was found a scroll in which these matters were recorded.
6.24: In the first year of the reign of Koresh, meleḵ Koresh ordered that the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 at Yerushalayim should be built again, where they offer with continual fire;
6.25: the height of which shall be sixty ammah and the width sixty ammah, with three rows of hewn stones, and one row of new wood from the land; and the expenses of it to be given out of the house of meleḵ Koresh;
6.26: and that the qodesh vessels of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, both of gold and silver, that Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar took out of the House at Yerushalayim, and brought to Baḇel, should be restored to the House at Yerushalayim, and be put in the place where they were before.
6.27: And he also commanded that Tattenai the governor of Suria and Phoinikĕ, and Shethar-Bozenai, and their companions, and those who were appointed rulers in Suria and Phoinikĕ, should bear in mind not to strive with the place, but allow Zerubbaḇel, the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and governor of Yahuḏah, and the elders of the Yahuḏim, to build the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in that place.
6.28: I have also commanded to have it built up complete again; and that they look diligently to help those who are of the captivity of the Yahuḏim, till the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is finished;
6.29: and out of the tribute of Koĕlĕ-Suria and Phoinikĕ a portion diligently to be given to these men for the slaughterings of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, that is, to Zerubbaḇel the governor; for bulls and rams and lambs;
6.30: and also corn, salt, wine and oil, and continually every year without further question, what is required by the kohenim who are in Yerushalayim to be used daily;
6.31: that offerings may be made to the Most High Elohim for the meleḵ and for his children, and that they may pray for their lives.
6.32: And he commanded that whoever would transgress, or even diminish any word spoken or written before, a timber should be taken out of his own house, and he be hanged upon it, and all his goods seized for the meleḵ.
6.33: Therefore may 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, whose Name is called upon there, utterly destroy every meleḵ and nation, that stretches out his hand to hinder or damage the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in Yerushalayim.
6.34: I, Dareyawesh the meleḵ have ordained that it be done according to these words with diligence.

7.1: Then following the commands of meleḵ Dareyawesh, Tattenai the governor of Koĕlĕ-Suria and Phoinikĕ, and Shethar-Bozenai, with their companions,
7.2: oversaw the qodesh works, diligently assisting the elders of the Yahuḏim and governors of the Hĕyḵal.
7.3: And so the qodesh works prospered, when Ḥaggai and Zeḵaryah the neḇi’im naḇa.
7.4: And they completed these by the Command of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, and with the consent of Koresh, Dareyawesh, and Artaḥshashta, melaḵim of Paras;
7.5: and so, the Qodesh House was finished in the twenty-third day of the month Aḏar, in the sixth year of Dareyawesh meleḵ of Paras.
7.6: And the children of Yisra’ĕl, the kohenim and the Lĕwites and others who were of the captivity that were added to them, did according to the words written in the Book of Mosheh.
7.7: And for the dedication of the Hĕyḵal of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 they offered a hundred bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs
7.8: and twelve goats for the sin of all Yisra’ĕl, according to the number of the heads of the tribes of Yisra’ĕl.
7.9: The kohenim and the Lĕwites also stood dressed in their garments, according to their clans, in the service of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, according to the Book of Mosheh; and the gatekeepers at every gate.
7.10: And the children of Yisra’ĕl who were of the captivity held the Pesaḥ the fourteenth day of the first month, after the kohenim and the Lĕwites were qadosh.
7.11: Those who were of the captivity were not all qadosh together; but the Lĕwites were all qadosh together,
7.12: and so they offered the Pesaḥ for all those of the captivity, and for their brothers the kohenim, and for themselves.
7.13: And the children of Yisra’ĕl that came out of the captivity ate, even all those who had separated themselves from the abominations of the people of the land, and sought 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
7.14: And they performed the Feast of Matstsoth seven days, rejoicing before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
7.15: for He had turned the counsel of the meleḵ of Ashshur toward them, to strengthen their hands in the works of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl.

8.1: And after these matters, when Artaḥshashta the meleḵ of Paras reigned, Ezra came, the son of Serayah, the son of Azaryah, the son of Ḥilqiyahu, the son of Shallum,
8.2: the son of Tsaḏoq, the son of Aḥituḇ, the son of Amaryah, the son of Azaryah, the son of Merayoth, the son of Zeraḥyah, the son of Uzzi, the son of Buqqi, the son of Aḇishua, the son of Pineḥas, the son of Eli’ezer, the son of Aharon the chief kohĕn.
8.3: This Ezra went up from Baḇel, as a scribe, being very skilled in the Law of Mosheh, that was given by the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl.
8.4: And the meleḵ esteemed him; for he found favor in his sight in all his requests.
8.5: There also went up with him to Yerushalayim, some of the children of Yisra’ĕl, of the kohenim of the Lĕwites, of the qodesh singers, gatekeepers and servants of the Hĕyḵal,
8.6: in the seventh year of the reign of Artaḥshashta, in the fifth month. This was the meleḵ’s seventh year; for they went from Baḇel in the first day of the first month, and came to Yerushalayim, according to the prosperous journey which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 gave them.
8.7: For Ezra had such great knowledge, that he omitted naught from the Torah and Commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, but taught all Yisra’ĕl the Torot and Right-Rulings.
8.8: Now the copy of the commission, which was written from Artaḥshashta the meleḵ, and came to Ezra the kohĕn and reader of the Torah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, is as follows:
8.9: meleḵ Artaḥshashta, to Ezra the kohĕn and reader of the Torah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, greetings.
8.10: Having determined to deal favorably, I have given an order, that those of the nation of the Yahuḏim and of the kohenim and Lĕwites being within our reign, who desire and are willing, should go with you to Yerushalayim.
8.11: As many therefore as have a heart to do so, let them depart with you, as it has seemed good both to me and my seven friends the counsellors;
8.12: that they may look to the affairs of Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim, agreeable to that which is in the Torah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄;
8.13: and carry the gifts to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of Yisra’ĕl to Yerushalayim, which I and my friends have vowed, and all the gold and silver that is found in the land of Baḇel, to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in Yerushalayim;
8.14: also with that which is given from the people for the Hĕyḵal of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 their Elohim at Yerushalayim; and that silver and gold may be collected for bulls, rams, and lambs, and matters pertaining to it;
8.15: so that they may offer slaughterings to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 upon the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 their Elohim, which is in Yerushalayim.
8.16: And whatever you and your brothers do with the silver and gold, do so according to the desire of your Elohim.
8.17: And the qodesh vessels of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, which have been given to you for the use of the Hĕyḵal of your Elohim, which is in Yerushalayim, you shall put before your Elohim in Yerushalayim;
8.18: and whatever else you shall remember for the use of the Hĕyḵal of your Elohim, you shall give it out of the meleḵ’s treasury.
8.19: And I meleḵ Artaḥshashta have also commanded the keepers of the treasuries in Suria and Phoinikĕ, that whatever Ezra the kohĕn and the reader of the Torah of the Most High Elohim shall send for, they should give it to him with haste,
8.20: to the sum of one hundred kiḵars of silver, likewise also of wheat even to a hundred kors, and a hundred baths of wine, and other matters in abundance.
8.21: Let all be performed after the Torah of Elohim diligently unto the Most High Elohim, so that wrath does not come upon the reign of the meleḵ and his sons.
8.22: I also command you, that you require no tax, nor any other tribute from any of the kohenim, or Lĕwites, or qodesh singers, or gatekeepers, or servants of the Hĕyḵal, or from any who are employed in this Hĕyḵal, and that no man has authority to impose any matter upon them.
8.23: And you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of Elohim, appoint judges and Right-Rulings, that they may judge in all Suria and Phoinikĕ all those who know the Torah of your Elohim; and those who do not know it, you shall teach;
8.24: and whoever transgresses the Torah of your Elohim, and of the meleḵ, shall be strictly punished, whether it be by death, or other punishment, by penalty of silver, or by imprisonment.
8.25: Then Ezra the scribe said, “Baruḵ be the only Aḏon, Elohim of my fathers, who has put these into the heart of the meleḵ, to esteem His House that is in Yerushalayim,
8.26: and has esteemed me in the sight of the meleḵ, and his counsellors, and all his friends and nobles.”
8.27: Therefore I was encouraged with the help of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 my Elohim, and gathered together men of Yisra’ĕl to go up with me.
8.28: And these are the heads according to their families and several nobles, that went up with me from Baḇel in the reign of meleḵ Artaḥshashta:
8.29: Of the sons of Pineḥas, Gĕreshon; of the sons of Ithamar, Dani’ĕl; of the sons of Dawiḏ, Ḥattush the son of Sheḵanyah;
8.30: of the sons of Perets, Zeḵaryah; and a hundred and fifty men were counted with him.
8.31: Of the sons of Paḥath-Mo’aḇ, Elyaho’ĕynai, the son of Zeraḥyah, and two hundred men with him.
8.32: Of the sons of Zattu, Sheḵanyah the son of Yaḥazi’ĕl, and with him three hundred men. Of the sons of Aḏin, Oḇĕḏ the son of Yahonathan, and two hundred and fifty men with him.
8.33: Of the sons of Ĕylam, Yoshiyahu son of Geḏalyahu, and seventy men with him.
8.34: Of the sons of Shephatyah, Tseruyah son of Miḵa’ĕl, and seventy men with him.
8.35: Of the sons of Yo’aḇ, Oḇaḏyah son of Yizli’ah, and two hundred and twelve men with him.
8.36: Of the sons of Shelomith, the son of Yosiphyah, and a hundred and sixty men with him.
8.37: Of the sons of Bĕḇai, Zeḵaryah son of Bĕḇai, and twenty-eight men with him.
8.38: Of the sons of Azgaḏ, Yoḥanan son of Haqqatan, and a hundred and ten men with him.
8.39: Of the sons of Aḏoniqam the last, and these are the names of them: Eliphelet, Ye’i’ĕl, and Shemayah, and seventy men with them.
8.40: Of the sons of Biḡwai, Uthai the son of Zabbuḏ, and seventy men with him.
8.41: And I gathered these together to the river called Ahawa, where we pitched our tents for three days; and then I inspected them.
8.42: But when I had found there none of the kohenim and Lĕwites,
8.43: then I sent to Eli’ezer, and Deu’ĕl, and Mishmannah,
8.44: and Elnathan, and Shemayah, and Yoyariḇ, and Nathan, Yahonathan, Zeḵaryah, and Meshullam, leaders and learned.
8.45: And I told them that they should go to Iddo the captain, who was treasurer in the place;
8.46: and ordered them that they should speak to Iddo, and to his brothers, and to the treasurers in that place, to send us such men who might execute the office of the kohenim in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
8.47: And by the mighty hand of our Aḏon they brought to us skilled men of the sons of Maḥli the son of Lĕwi, the son of Yisra’ĕl: Shĕrĕḇyah, and his sons, and his brothers, eighteen.
8.48: And Ḥashaḇyah, and Bani, and Hoshĕa his brother, of the sons of Ḥananyah, and their sons, were twenty men.
8.49: And of the servants of the Hĕyḵal whom Dawiḏ had appointed, and the leaders of the service of the Lĕwites, that is, the servants of the Hĕyḵal: two hundred and twenty, the list of whose names were shown.
8.50: And there I proclaimed a fast to the young men before our Aḏon, to seek from Him a prosperous journey for both us and they who were with us, for our children, and for the cattle;
8.51: for I was ashamed to ask from the meleḵ footmen and horsemen and conduct for safeguard against our adversaries.
8.52: For we had said to the meleḵ, that the power of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim would be with those who seek Him, to support them in all ways.
8.53: And again we sought our Aḏon regarding these, and found Him favorable to us.
8.54: Then I separated twelve of the heads of the kohenim, Shĕrĕḇyah, and Ḥashaḇyah, and ten men of their brothers with them;
8.55: and I weighed them the gold, and silver, and the qodesh vessels of the House of our Aḏon, which the meleḵ and his council and the princes, and all Yisra’ĕl, had given.
8.56: And when I had weighed it, I gave six hundred and fifty kiḵars of silver to them, and silver vessels of a hundred kiḵars, and a hundred kiḵars of gold,
8.57: and twenty golden vessels, and twelve vessels of bronze, even of fine bronze, glittering like gold.
8.58: And I said to them, “Both you and the vessels are qodesh to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and the gold and the silver is vowed to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Aḏon of our fathers.
8.59: “Watch, and guard them till you deliver them to the heads of the kohenim and the Lĕwites, and to the leaders of the families of Yisra’ĕl, in Yerushalayim, into the rooms of the House of our Elohim.”
8.60: So the kohenim and the Lĕwites, who had received the silver and gold and the vessels, brought them to Yerushalayim, into the Hĕyḵal of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
8.61: And from the River Ahawa we departed the twelfth day of the first month, and came to Yerushalayim by the mighty hand of our Aḏon, who was with us; and from the beginning of our journey 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 delivered us from every enemy, and so we came to Yerushalayim.
8.62: And when we had been there three days, the gold and silver that was weighed was delivered on the fourth day into the House of our Aḏon, to Merĕmoth the kohĕn, the son of Uriyah.
8.63: And with him was Eli’ezer the son of Pineḥas, and with them were Yozaḇaḏ the son of Yĕshua and No’aḏyah the son of Binnui, Lĕwites - all was delivered to them by number and weight,
8.64: and all the weight of them was recorded that same hour.
8.65: And those who were come out of the captivity brought an offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, even twelve bulls for all Yisra’ĕl, ninety-six rams,
8.66: seventy-two lambs, twelve goats for a peace offering; all of them slaughterings to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
8.67: And they delivered the meleḵ’s orders to the meleḵ’s trustees and to the governors of Koĕlĕ-Suria and Phoinikĕ; and they esteemed the people and the Hĕyḵal of Elohim.
8.68: Now when these matters were done, the rulers came to me, and said,
8.69: “The nation of Yisra’ĕl, the princes, the kohenim and Lĕwites, have not put away the foreigners of the land from them, nor the defilements of the gentiles that is, of the Kena’anites, Ḥittites, Perizzites, Yeḇusites, and the Mo’aḇites, Mitsrites, and Eḏomites.
8.70: For both they and their sons have married with their daughters, and the qodesh seed is mixed with the foreigners of the land; and from the beginning, the rulers and the great men have taken part in this wickedness.”
8.71: And as soon as I had heard this, I tore my garments, and the qodesh garment, and pulled the hair from my head and beard, and sat down grieved and very heavy.
8.72: So all those who were then moved at the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl assembled to me, while I mourned for the wickedness; but I sat full of heaviness until the evening offering.
8.73: Then rising from the fast with my garments and the qodesh garment torn and bowing my knees and stretching out my hands to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
8.74: I said, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, I am disappointed and ashamed before Your face;
8.75: for our sins have multiplied above our heads, and our ignorances have reached up to the shamayim.
8.76: “For ever since the time of our fathers we have been and are in great sin, even to this day.
8.77: “And for ours and our fathers’ sins, we with our brothers and our melaḵim and our kohenim were given up to the melaḵim of the earth, to the sword, and to captivity, and for a prey with shame, unto this day.
8.78: “And now in some measure, kindness has been shown to us from You, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, that there should be left to us a root and a name in the place of Your Miqdash;
8.79: and to uncover for us a light in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim, and to give us food in the time of our service.
8.80: “Indeed, when we were in bondage, we were not forsaken by our Aḏon; but He made us favorable before the melaḵim of Paras, so that they gave us food;
8.81: and also esteemed the Hĕyḵal of our Aḏon, and raised up Tsiyon that was laid waste, and they have given us a permanent place in Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim.
8.82: “And now, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, what shall we say, having these? For we have transgressed Your Commands, which You gave by the hand of Your servants the neḇi’im, saying,
8.83: ‘The land, which you enter in to possess as an inheritance, is a land defiled with the abominations of the gentiles of the land, and they have filled it with their uncleanness.
8.84: ‘Now therefore, you shall not join your daughters unto their sons, neither shall you take their daughters for your sons.
8.85: ‘And you shall never seek to have peace with them, that you may be strong, and eat the good of the land, and that you leave the inheritance of the land to your children forever.’
8.86: “And all that has come to be has been done to us because of our wicked works and great sins! And You, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, lifted our sins,
8.87: and gave to us a root, but we have turned back again to transgress Your Torah, and to mingle ourselves with the uncleanness of the nations of the land.
8.88: “Were You not wroth with us to destroy us, till You had left us neither root, seed nor name?
8.89: “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of Yisra’ĕl, You are true! For we are left a root this day.
8.90: “See, we are now before You in our wickednesses, for we cannot stand any longer by reason of these matters before You.”
8.91: And as Ezra made his confession in his prayer, weeping and lying flat on the ground before the Hĕyḵal, a very great crowd of men, women and children there gathered to him from Yerushalayim; for there was great weeping among the crowd.
8.92: Then Sheḵanyah the son of Yeḥi’ĕl, one of the sons of Yisra’ĕl, called out, and said, “O Ezra, we have sinned against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim, we have married foreign women of the nations of the land, but now there is expectancy for all Yisra’ĕl!
8.93: “Let us make an oath to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, that we shall put away all our wives which we have taken from the gentiles, with their children,
8.94: as you have said, and as many who obey the Torah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
8.95: “Arise and act on this; for this is your word, and we shall be with you. Be strong.”
8.96: So Ezra arose, and made the chief of the kohenim and Lĕwites of all Yisra’ĕl swear to do after these matters; and so they swore.

9.1: Then rising from the court of the Hĕyḵal, Ezra went to the room of Yoḥanan the son of Elyashiḇ,
9.2: and remained there, and ate no bread nor drank water, mourning for the great wickednesses of the multitude.
9.3: And there was a call in all Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim to all those who were of the captivity, that they should be gathered together at Yerushalayim;
9.4: and that whoever did not meet there within two or three days according to when the ruling elders appointed, their cattle should be seized for the use of the Hĕyḵal, and himself thrown out from those who were of the captivity.
9.5: And in three days, all those of the tribe of Yahuḏah and Binyamin were gathered together at Yerushalayim, the twentieth day of the ninth month.
9.6: And all the crowd sat shivering in the outer court of the Hĕyḵal because of the bad weather present.
9.7: So Ezra arose up, and said to them, “You have transgressed the Torah in marrying foreign wives, and so have increased the sins of Yisra’ĕl.
9.8: “And now in confessing, give esteem to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of our fathers,
9.9: and do His desire, and separate yourselves from the gentiles of the land, and from the foreign women.”
9.10: Then the whole crowd spoke, and cried with a loud voice, “As you have spoken, so we shall do!
9.11: “But because the people are many, and it is bad weather, we cannot stand in the open, and this is not a work of a day or two, seeing our sin in this has spread far;
9.12: therefore let the rulers of the multitude stay, and let all those of our dwellings who have foreign wives come at the time appointed,
9.13: and the rulers and judges of every place with them, till we turn away the wrath of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 from us for this matter.”
9.14: Then Yahonathan son of Asah’ĕl and Yaḥzeyah son of Tiqwah opposed this matter upon them, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Lĕwite supported them.
9.15: But those who were of the captivity did according to all these matters.
9.16: And Ezra the kohĕn chose for himself the leaders of their families, all by name; and on the first day of the tenth month they sat together to examine the matter.
9.17: So the cases of those who held foreign wives was brought to an end on the first day of the first month.
9.18: And the kohenim who had come together, and found to have foreign wives were:
9.19: Of the sons of Yĕshua son of Yotsaḏaq, and his brothers; Ma’asĕyah and Eli’ezer, and Yariḇ and Geḏalyahu.
9.20: And they gave their hand to put away their wives and to offer rams to make atonement for their sins.
9.21: And of the sons of Immĕr; Ḥanani, and Zeḇaḏyah, and Ma’asĕyah, and Shemayah, and Yeḥi’ĕl, and Uzziyah.
9.22: And of the sons of Pashḥur; Elyo’ĕynai, Ma’asĕyah, Yishma’ĕl, and Nethan’ĕl, and Yozaḇaḏ and El’asah.
9.23: And of the Lĕwites: Yozaḇaḏ, and Shim’i, and Qĕlayah, who was called Qelita, and Pethaḥyah, and Yahuḏah, and Eli’ezer.
9.24: Of the qodesh singers: Elyashiḇ, and Zakkur.
9.25: Of the gatekeepers; Shallum, and Telem.
9.26: Of those of Yisra’ĕl, of the sons of Parosh: Ramyah, and Yizziyah, and Malkiyah, and Miyamin, and El’azar, and Malkiyah, and Benayah.
9.27: Of the sons of Ĕylam: Mattanyah, Zeḵaryah, and Aḇdi, and Yerĕmoth, and Ĕliyahu.
9.28: And of the sons of Zattu: Elyo’ĕynai, Elyashiḇ, Mattanyah, Yerĕmoth, and Zaḇaḏ, and Aziza.
9.29: Of the sons of Bĕḇai; Yahoḥanan, and Ḥananyah and Zabbai, and Athlai.
9.30: Of the sons of Bani: Meshullam, Malluḵ, Aḏayah, Yashuḇ, She’al, and Ramoth.
9.31: And of the sons of Paḥath-Mo’aḇ; Aḏna, and Ma’asĕyah, Kelal, and Benayah, and Mattanyah, and Betsal’ĕl, Binnui, and Menashsheh.
9.32: And of the sons of Ḥarim; Eli’ezer and Yishshiyah, and Malkiyah, and Shemayah, and Shim’on.
9.33: And of the sons of Ḥashum; Mattenai, and Mattattah, and Zaḇaḏ, Eliphelet, and Yirmeyah, Menashsheh, and Shim’i.
9.34: And of the sons of Bani; Ma’aḏai, Amram, U’ĕl, Benayah, and Bĕḏeyah, and Wanyah, Merĕmoth, and Elyashiḇ, and Mattenai, Ya’asu, Bani, Binnui, Shim’i, Shelemyah, Nathan. And of the sons of Ezra; Shashai, Azar’ĕl, Azi’ĕl, Shemaryah, Amaryah, Yosĕph.
9.35: And of the sons of Neḇo; Mattithyah, Zaḇaḏ, Yaddu, Yo’ĕl, Benayah.
9.36: All these had taken foreign wives, and they put them away with their children.
9.37: And the kohenim and Lĕwites, and those who were of Yisra’ĕl, dwelt in Yerushalayim, and in the land on the first day of the seventh month; so the children of Yisra’ĕl were in their dwellings.
9.38: And the whole crowd came together with one accord into the open place of the qodesh porch toward the east;
9.39: and they spoke to Ezra the kohĕn and reader, to bring the Torah of Mosheh, that was given of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl.
9.40: So Ezra the chief kohĕn brought the Torah to the whole crowd from man to woman, and to all the kohenim, to hear the Torah on the first day of the seventh month.
9.41: And he read in the open court before the qodesh porch from morning to noon, before both men and women; and the crowd gave heed to the Torah.
9.42: And Ezra the kohĕn and reader of the Torah stood up on a wooden platform, which was made for that purpose.
9.43: And beside him stood Mattithyah, Shema, Anayah, Azaryah, Uriyah, Ḥilqiyahu, Ma’asĕyah, on the right hand;
9.44: And on his left hand stood Peḏayah, Misha’ĕl, Malkiyah, Ḥashum, and Ḥashbaddanah and Zeḵaryah.
9.45: Then Ezra took the Book of the Torah before the crowd - for he sat esteemed at the head in the sight of them all -
9.46: and when he opened the Torah, they all stood straight up. So Ezra baraḵ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim Most High, the Elohim of hosts, Almighty.
9.47: And all the people answered, “Amĕn!” And lifting up their hands they fell to the ground, and worshipped 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
9.48: Also Yĕshua, Bani, Shĕrĕḇyah, Yamin, Aqquḇ, Shabbethai, Hoḏiyah, Ma’asĕyah, and Qelita, Azaryah, and Yozaḇaḏ, and Ḥanan, Pelayah, the Lĕwites, taught the Torah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, making them all to understand it.
9.49: Then the governor spoke to Ezra the chief kohĕn and reader, and to the Lĕwites that taught the crowd, even to all, saying,
9.50: “This day is qodesh to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.” - For they all wept when they heard the Torah -
9.51: “Go then, and eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions to those who have none;
9.52: for this day is qodesh to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and be not sorrowful; for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall exalt you.”
9.53: So the Lĕwites proclaimed to all the people saying, “This day is qodesh to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄; do not be sorrowful.”
9.54: Then they went their way, every one to eat and drink, and be joyful, and to give portions to those who had none, and to rejoice;
9.55: because they understood the Words in which they were instructed, and for the reason they had been assembled.
